{{Short description|Romanian astronomer and mathematician (1832–1915)}}
[[File:Neculai Culianu.jpg|thumb|Nicolae Culianu]]
'''Nicolae Culianu''' (28 August 1832 – 28 November 1915) was a [[Moldavia]]n, later [[Romania]]n mathematician and astronomer.

A native of [[Iași]], he enrolled in the [[University of Paris]] after graduating from ''[[Academia Mihăileană]]'' in 1855, and earned his undergraduate degree in mathematics in 1860. He remained there until 1863, performing research at the [[Paris Observatory]].<ref name="ieseni">{{in lang|ro}} Ciprian Teodorescu, [http://bjiasi.ro/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/ACADEMICIENI-IESENI.pdf ''Academicieni ieșeni''], p. 124, at the Gheorghe Asachi Iași County library site</ref> Initially a high school teacher,<ref name="o307">Ornea, p. 307</ref> he later joined the astronomy and geodesy faculty of the [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University|University of Iași]],<ref name="ieseni"/><ref name="oc"/> where he served as dean of the sciences faculty, and from 1880 to 1898 as [[Rector (academia)|rector]].<ref name="oc"/><ref name="d">Diaconu, pp. 129–30</ref> He was a close associate of [[Titu Maiorescu]], a member of the ''[[Junimea]]'' movement that the latter led, and involved in the educational reform movement it promoted. As such, he was among the founders of a private high school in Iași, to which he donated a group of buildings.<ref name="oc"/> While active in ''Junimea'', his renowned affability and venerable bearing earned him the nickname "Papa Culiano".<ref name="o307"/> He was elected a corresponding [[list of members of the Romanian Academy|member of the Romanian Academy]] in 1889.<ref>{{in lang|ro}} [http://www.acad.ro/bdar/armembriLit.php?vidT=C Membrii Academiei Române din 1866 până în prezent] at the Romanian Academy site</ref>

He helped found the Iași astronomical observatory for the use of students and teachers, and published textbooks on mathematics and geodesy.<ref name="oc"/> He was among the founders ''{{ill|Recreații Științifice|ro}}'', the country's first scientific periodical addressed to young people and to a generalist audience.<ref name="ieseni"/><ref name="d"/> Briefly involved in politics, he was vice president of the [[Romanian Senate]] during the fourth [[Conservative Party (Romania, 1880–1918)|conservative]] government of [[Lascăr Catargiu]] (1892–1896).<ref name="ieseni"/><ref name="oc">{{in lang|ro}} Tereza Culianu-Petrescu, [http://www.observatorcultural.ro/O-biografie*articleID_989-articles_details.html "O biografie"], ''[[Observator Cultural]]'', nr. 87, October 2001</ref>

Culianu's textbooks include an 1870 one on differential and integral calculus, the first published Romanian-language course on mathematical analysis; and ones on elementary algebra (1872), applied geometry (1874), plane and spherical trigonometry (1875), cosmography (1893), plane trigonometry (1894), and high-school cosmography (1895).<ref name="ieseni"/> He was buried in [[Eternitatea cemetery|Eternitatea Cemetery]].<ref name="b">{{in lang|ro}} Temistocle Bîrsan, [http://www.recreatiimatematice.ro/arhiva/miscelannea/RM12011CLIMESCU.pdf "Restaurarea mormântului lui C. Climescu, fost rector al Universității din Iași"], in ''Recreații Matematice'', nr.1/2011, pp. 3–4</ref> His great-grandson was [[Ioan Petru Culianu]].<ref name="oc"/>
